title: SDK edge adapters and offline resilience playbook
author: Aisha Thompson
body:
Overview

This playbook describes recommended SDK adapter patterns and operational guidance for building resilient client integrations that tolerate intermittent connectivity, operate in offline-first contexts, and degrade gracefully while preserving telemetry and cost signals. It complements runtime-side patterns (redwood-runtime and redwood-proxy) by focusing on client-side components used by product teams and integrators.

Scope and audience

- Intended for SDK engineers, integrators, and platform engineers who embed Redwood SDKs in web/mobile/edge clients.
- Covers adapter patterns (caching, queuing, network fallbacks), configuration templates, tests, rollout guidance, and triage/playbook for common failure modes.
- Not a replacement for server-side SLOs and capacity playbooks; see runtime and SRE docs for server-side controls.

TL;DR recommendations

1) Provide a small, well-documented adapter surface on each SDK so integrators can opt into offline/resilient behavior. Default: disabled for hosted-critical paths; opt-in for edge/embedded use.
2) Implement three composable adapters: cache-adapter, queue-adapter, and network-adapter. Keep them pluggable and testable.
3) Preserve observability: emit retry/drop events and sampled request bodies to the local telemetry buffer with strict PII filters.
4) Use deterministic backoff and jitter policies; avoid unbounded retries that cause request storms on reconnection.

Adapter reference patterns

1) Cache-adapter (prefix/prompt caching)
- Purpose: return cached responses for stable prompt templates or previously evaluated prefixes when network unavailable or to reduce token usage.
- Behavior: TTL-based entries, optional fuzzy-match for near-identical prompts, KV cache pluggable to local storage (IndexedDB, SQLite, platform-backed).
- Deterministic keys: hash(prompt_template + canonicalized_inputs + model_id + max_tokens + quantization_profile).

2) Queue-adapter (local enqueue & durable delivery)
- Purpose: accept requests when offline and deliver when connectivity restored. Support ordered and idempotent delivery.
- Persistent store: SQLite on mobile/desktop, local files on embedded Linux, or IndexedDB on web.
- Delivery modes: background-push (preferred) and foreground-drain (fallback).

3) Network-adapter (multi-route fallback + preflight)
- Purpose: select best endpoint with graceful fallbacks (region, dedicated vs hosted, edge proxy).
- Preflight: light HEAD/TCP probe to chosen endpoint and measure latency; switch to alternate endpoints on sustained failures.
- Fallback policy config: prefer dedicated endpoints within 100ms baseline, otherwise route to hosted with small token-rate limits.

Example architecture diagram (textual)

Client app -> SDK core -> [cache-adapter] -> [queue-adapter] -> [network-adapter] -> redwood-proxy -> redwood-runtime

Configuration schema (YAML example)

```
# sdk-resilience-config.yaml
adapters:
  cache:
    enabled: true
    backend: "indexeddb"
    ttl_seconds: 86400
    fuzzy_match: false
  queue:
    enabled: true
    backend: "sqlite"
    max_queue_items: 500
    delivery_mode: "background-push"
  network:
    probes_per_endpoint: 3
    preflight_interval_seconds: 30
    failover_threshold: 0.2   # fraction of failed probes
retry_policy:
  max_attempts: 5
  base_backoff_ms: 300
  max_backoff_ms: 10000
  jitter: 0.2
telemetry:
  sample_rate: 0.02
  local_buffer_size: 1000
  pii_filters: ["email", "ssn"]
```

JavaScript adapter usage (example)

```
import { RedwoodSDK, SQLiteQueueAdapter, IndexedDBCacheAdapter } from '@redwood/sdk';

const sdk = new RedwoodSDK({
  networkAdapter: { endpoints: ["https://us1.redwood.ai", "https://eu1.redwood.ai"], preflight: true },
  cacheAdapter: new IndexedDBCacheAdapter({ ttlSeconds: 86400 }),
  queueAdapter: new SQLiteQueueAdapter({ maxItems: 200 })
});

// Send a request that will be queued if offline
const resp = await sdk.generate({ model: 'gptx-small', prompt: 'Summarize Q1 results' });
```

Python example (background delivery)

```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
from redwood.adapters import FileQueueAdapter, MemoryCacheAdapter

cfg = {
  'queue': FileQueueAdapter('/var/tmp/rw_queue.db'),
  'cache': MemoryCacheAdapter(ttl_seconds=3600),
  'network': { 'endpoints': ['https://us1.redwood.ai'] }
}
client = RedwoodClient(config=cfg)

# enqueue; returns a request id
req_id = client.generate_async('gptx-small', 'Draft an email subject')
```

Operational controls and telemetry

Required telemetry events (all adapters must emit):
- adapter.queue.enqueued (tags: adapter, queue_length, request_size_bytes)
- adapter.queue.sent (tags: adapter, request_age_seconds, success)
- adapter.cache.hit/miss (tags: adapter, key_hash)
- adapter.network.probe (tags: endpoint, latency_ms, success)
- adapter.retry.attempt (tags: attempt, backoff_ms)
- adapter.drop (tags: reason, last_error_code)

SLOs and thresholds for SDK behavior (recommended):
- Max local queue age: 24h (requests older than this should be expired and emitted as adapter.drop with reason=stale).
- Queue persistence success: >= 99.5% writes under normal device conditions.
- Telemetry delivery: best-effort; SDK must batch and backoff to avoid CPU/network spikes.

Testing and validation checklist

1) Unit tests for adapter logic (cache key determinism, queue ordering, idempotency).
2) Integration tests that simulate offline and reconnection windows at multiple latencies. Include tests for partial failure of endpoints and prioritized failover.
3) End-to-end contract tests that validate telemetry events are emitted and PII filters applied.
4) Chaos test: simulate storage full, permission errors, and abrupt process termination to verify no data corruption and safe expiration.

Rollout and migration guidance

1) Feature gate: release adapters behind an opt-in feature flag in SDK minor releases.
2) Canary: enable adapters for 1–2 customers or internal beta for 2 weeks, monitor telemetry (adapter.queue.sent/adapter.drop) and device metrics (disk usage, CPU).
3) Gradual rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3–4 weeks with automated rollback on adapter.drop spike > 2x baseline.
4) Migration path: if switching cache backends (e.g., memory -> sqlite), provide a transition mode that reads fallback from old backend for 7 days and emits migration_summary telemetry.

Troubleshooting matrix

| Symptom | Likely cause | Diagnostic step | Remediation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Requests never leave client queue | Persistent connectivity failure OR malformed endpoint config | Inspect local queue length, run preflight probe: `rwctl probe endpoint` | Surface user-facing status, allow manual drain, advise reconnect or switch endpoint |
| Large number of adapter.drop with reason=quota | Endpoint rate limit or server-side quota | Check adapter.network.probe success and server 429 responses | Backoff, offer degrade mode (local-only responses), and request quota increase |
| Telemetry missing from device | Telemetry buffer full or PII filter blocking | Check local telemetry buffer size and sample_rate | Increase local_buffer_size or reduce sample_rate temporarily; ensure filters are correct |
| Data corruption after crash | Unhandled write concurrency in queue backend | Run queue integrity check `rwctl queue-check /path` | Fix adapter to use safe transactional writes; document in release notes |

CLI troubleshooting helpers (examples)

- Probe endpoints: `rwctl probe --endpoint https://us1.redwood.ai --count 5`
- Inspect local queue: `rwctl queue-list --db /path/to/queue.db --limit 50`
- Drain queue manually: `rwctl queue-drain --db /path/to/queue.db --target https://us1.redwood.ai`
- Telemetry buffer dump (sanitized): `rwctl telemetry-dump --sanitized --limit 200`

Security and privacy guardrails

- PII: local adapters must apply a PII filter before storing any request payload. PII filters are configured centrally; SDKs must support dynamic filter updates pulled from a redwood-policy endpoint.
- Encryption: persistent adapter storage must be encrypted at rest (platform mechanism or library-level encryption). For web (IndexedDB) use WebCrypto-based encryption shim.
- Consent: mobile/embedded SDKs must respect user privacy settings (opt-out disables telemetry sampling and local persistence).

Appendix: quick reference snippets

- Deterministic cache key (pseudo): `sha256(model_id + '::' + normalize(prompt) + '::' + params)`
- Recommended backoff sequence: 300ms, 600ms, 1200ms, 2400ms, 4800ms (+jitter)

FAQ

Q: Should adapters be enabled by default?
A: No. Default should be safe (no local persistence) for most production hosted customers. Enable adapters by configuration and clearly document behaviour.

Q: How do we avoid double-delivery on reconnection?
A: Use idempotency keys (client generated UUID per logical request) and server-side idempotency support where possible. Queue adapter should store idempotency key with the entry.
